question:
Unit: one return filed this year
Target: whether an examination changes the tax, yes or no
Time: returns filed this year, ranked now; past examinations to learn from
items:
| Item | Kind | Question it serves | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wages on the return | the return's lines | Did the return report all its wages? | needed | A first model starts with what the taxpayer reported directly. |
| Total income on the return | the return's lines | How much income did the return report? | needed | It is the line item the question depends on most. |
| Taxpayer name and identifying number | the return's lines | none | not needed | It names the taxpayer and tells the ranking nothing it needs. |
| Wages that employers reported | data to match against | Do the reported wages match what employers sent? | needed | A gap between the return and the payers is a reason to look. |
| Interest that banks reported | data to match against | Does the reported interest match what banks sent? | needed | The same match as wages, for interest income. |
| Whether a past examination changed the tax | past outcomes | What happened when a return like this was examined? | needed | It is the target the model learns from. |
| How the IRS selected each examined return | past outcomes | Which outcomes stand for all returns? | needed | Outcomes a score chose leave out the returns it skipped. |
explain: Returns that a score chose show outcomes only for the returns the score already favoured, so a model trained on them never learns about the rest. The record of random sample or score lets the builders correct for that.
